sources.entry: Documenso - Digital document signing platform (alternative to DocuSign). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker
Documenso | Document signing platform, a DocuSign alternative

summary.one_liner: Documenso is an open-source digital document signing platform, positioned as an alternative to DocuSign, that can be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Documenso as an open-source DocuSign alternative for signing documents digitally, with the option to self-host it and review how it works. It is built with TypeScript, React Router v7, Hono, Prisma, and tRPC, with a Postgres database. The README names PDF handling libraries (@libpdf/core for PDF signatures, pdf.js for viewing, @cantoo/pdf-lib for manipulation) and react-email for email templates. Local development uses npm scripts (npm run dx starts a Postgres database and an Inbucket mail server in Docker, then npm run dev). Official Docker images are published on DockerHub and GitHub Container Registry, and the README lists Docker, Docker Compose, Railway, Kubernetes, and manual deployment options. The README says external pull requests are paused, so contributions are mainly through issues.
use_cases: run an open-source e-signature tool with auditable code
deploy document signing with Docker or Kubernetes
send documents for signature to others
notable: Self-hostable, with the README stating users can review how it works under the hood
Official Docker images on DockerHub and GitHub Container Registry
Supports Docker, Docker Compose, Railway, Kubernetes, and manual deployment
Dev quickstart spins up Postgres and an Inbucket mail server in Docker
Offers a hosted version at documenso.com and an Enterprise plan
caveats: The README says external pull requests are no longer accepted except from a small trusted group; contributions go through issues
Requires Node.js v24 or above and a Postgres database for local development
Enterprise plan is offered for large organizations, with details only via contact
